title: kovan-semantics: language-server integration (rust-analyzer first)

description:
HeatExchanger (components/heat_exchanger.rs:16) has area: Area -- but that is heat-TRANSFER surface area, not an envelope. A compact plate HX and a large shell-and-tube unit can share an area, so it cannot drive a faithful on-screen size on its own.

Needs a shell/footprint dimension alongside the existing area (keep the area -- it is real and used by the physics).

Part of op-dt3.17. The digital-twin widget layer must derive a component's on-screen size from its REAL dimensions; the engine crate forbids new physics, so the dimension must exist here in tampines.

DO NOT use HemSteamCv::get_volume() as a size -- it is the thermodynamic control volume, caller-supplied and unvalidated, conventionally a 1 m3 dummy (get_ref_vol() returns exactly 1.0 m3). It describes the fluid parcel, not the machine.

Prefer explicit named dimensions where shape matters to the drawing; a single nominal Volume is acceptable where only a rough size correlation is wanted. Document units and valid ranges in the doc comment per the workspace human-interface rule, and keep uom types.
title: tampines HeatExchanger: add envelope dimensions distinct from heat-transfer area

description:
op-t647 landed interfaces::checked on 2026-08-11 (commit 4feb6c84) covering 23 functions plus 2 public validators: the (T,p) single-phase family (11) and the (p,h) family (12). Deliberately left uncovered, each still panic-only:

- the (p,s) flash family
- the (h,s) flash family
- pt_flash_metastable
- the two-phase *_tp_eqm_two_phase(t,p,x) family
- alpha_v and kappa_t
- the OOP TampinesSteamTableCV surface
- the choked-flow solvers

Each has its own validity-range module, so each needs its own envelope gate rather than a shared one.

FOLLOW THE PATTERN ALREADY ESTABLISHED, which is the valuable part of op-t647: NO catch_unwind. The facade works by tracing every reachable panic in the wrapped call graph to a small number of envelope gates and excluding those cases before the internals run. That is why it is a bounds check and not an exception handler. It also caught NaN explicitly, because the internals range comparisons silently return false on NaN and would otherwise pass it straight through.

NOTE the interaction with the P1 router bug filed separately: p = 100 MPa exactly panics above 623.15 K because of a half-open range in the Region-2/Region-3 arms. Fix that first if possible, since otherwise every new gate has to encode the same exclusion as a workaround.
title: tampines-steam-tables: extend the bounds-checked facade to the remaining panicking entry points

description: Port Torus{X,Y,Z} CSG surfaces into outram-mc-libs geometry/surface.rs. Unlike the quadric surfaces (op-ah7), a torus is a QUARTIC surface, so ray-torus intersection needs a quartic root solver (Ferrari/companion-matrix) rather than the shared smallest_positive_root quadratic path. Mirror OpenMC SurfaceTorus (src/surface.cpp). Lower priority — tori are rarely used in reactor CSG.
title: outram-mc: port Torus{X,Y,Z} quartic CSG surfaces (needs quartic root solver)

description: Acceptance gate for the epic. On this repo's real history, the Rust implementation must produce byte-identical trailers and query totals to token_usage.py, and an equivalent historian report. Capture the Python output BEFORE deleting the scripts (needs a working python3 -- the Windows clone cannot run it, so this gate runs on Linux). Do NOT delete the Python until parity is demonstrated and recorded, per the V&V documentation rule: methodology AND measured results both go in the doc comment.
title: Parity tests: Rust output vs Python output

description: Wave 3 (after cyclic op-6w0.4). Non-conformal cyclic: compute AMI overlap/interpolation weights between two non-matching patch pairs and wire the weighted cross-boundary coupling into the FV matrix. Depends on cyclic face-pairing landing first (op-6w0.4). AMI weight computation (mesh/ami.rs) is the self-contained hard part; operator wiring shares files with cyclic. Cite OpenFOAM cyclicAMIPolyPatch / AMIInterpolation. V&V against a matching-mesh cyclic case (weights -> identity) + a known non-conformal overlap. Untrusted AI-assisted draft pending human V&V.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: cyclicAMI (non-conformal periodic, arbitrary mesh interface)

description:
37 lines. Draws one Color32::GRAY circle. NOTHING is state-derived: Pump::evaluate is inert so there is no live state, and Pump has no dimensions. Blocked on op-dt3.17.2 for size; a working evaluate would also give it something to show.

Quality bar: look derives from the component's real dimensions and live state, not from arbitrary screen coordinates; document units, valid ranges and what drives what in the /// doc comment; add tests; and per the workspace V&V rule state BOTH methodology and measured results where anything is checked against a reference. Do not fabricate a value to render -- an unpopulated component must be visibly distinct from a cold one (PipeVisual's neutral-grey empty case is the precedent).
title: Widget Studio QC: PumpVisual — currently a flat grey circle
